title: Create payment endpoint
content: POST /payments creates a payment for a customer. The request body requires amount (positive number) and currency (ISO 4217). On success the API returns 201 with a payment_id. Validation failures return 400; unauthorized callers receive 401.

title: Checkout with saved payment method
content: As a returning customer, I want to complete checkout with a saved payment method so that I can buy without re-entering card details. Acceptance: given a signed-in user with at least one saved method, when they confirm checkout, then the order is placed and a confirmation is shown.

title: Session cookie not cleared on logout
content: Expected: after logout the session cookie is removed and protected routes redirect to sign-in. Actual: the cookie remains and a refresh still shows the previous user. Steps: sign in, open /account, click Log out, refresh /account. Environment: Chromium, staging build 2026-08-20.

title: IngestKnowledge.execute orchestration
content: IngestKnowledge.execute accepts an IngestRequest of normalized SourceDocument values, rejects non-empty tickets until Ticket mapping ships, rejects duplicate SourceReference values, then chunks, embeds, deletes prior vectors for each source, and upserts the new chunks.

title: Authentication session lifetime
content: REQ-AUTH-12: Interactive user sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity. Renewing a session requires a valid refresh token issued at sign-in. Concurrent sessions for the same account are allowed unless the account is marked high-risk.

title: Severity versus priority in QA triage
content: Severity describes impact on users or the system if the defect is true: data loss and security issues are higher severity than cosmetic copy issues. Priority describes when to fix relative to release goals and workarounds. A medium-severity defect can be high priority before a launch; a high-severity defect with a safe workaround may wait. Record both fields separately so triage debates stay precise.
